result.title: IT policy: Suspected compromise
result.body:
Any one of these is a sign that an account may be compromised:
- 5 or more failed sign-ins in the last 24 hours from a country the employee has not signed in from before;
- an MFA device registered in the last 24 hours that the employee says they didn't add;
- an identity check where the employee, or their manager, says the employee didn't make this request: an
  `hr_callback` result `denied_request`, an `mfa_push` result `denied`, or a `manager_attestation` rejected for that
  reason.

If you see one:
- Stop, and use `escalate_to_security` for that employee.
- Take no other action on their account or access: no unlock, reset, MFA change, or group change.
- Set the ticket to `escalated`.
- You may tell the employee that Security will contact them.

result.title: IT policy: Verifying identity
result.body:
The chat system adds a line in square brackets to the first message. It shows either that the sender is **signed in**
as a named employee, or that they are writing from the **guest kiosk** (not signed in).

**Tier 1: signed in.** Being signed in is enough for questions, and for access, license, asset and change *requests*.
Those requests are gated by approvals instead.

**Tier 2** is required before any password reset (`reset_password`), unlock (`unlock_account`) or MFA reset
(`reset_mfa`), and before doing anything at all for someone writing from the guest kiosk. Tier 2 must be completed in
this conversation, using `verify_identity`, before the action. Only these results count:

| Method | Counts when |
|---|---|
| `mfa_push` | The push to an MFA device registered on the account returns `approved`. A push never counts for an MFA reset. |
| `hr_callback` | The callback to the mobile number on the HR record returns `confirmed`. |
| `manager_attestation` | The attestation request is `approved` by the person who would approve for the employee's manager under policy KB-P05 (normally the current manager). |

When tier 2 is needed, run one of these checks; don't turn the person away without trying one that is available.

Never enough, alone or together: employee ID, date of birth, manager's name, job title, or anything else that someone
else could know or look up.

Reset links (`reset_password`) go only to the mobile number or personal email on the employee's HR record (`hr_contact`).
Never send them anywhere else, whoever asks.

args.summary: Account E2901 (Brenda Walsh) locked for too many failed sign-ins. Matches KB-P12 compromise signs: 11 failed sign-ins 07:05-09:40 today (2026-10-28) from Bucharest, RO, a country with no prior sign-ins (usual sign-ins are Portland, US). Also an MFA device 'Android device' (MD-2901-2) was registered via self-service today at 08:02, which the employee has not confirmed adding. Unlock/reset/MFA changes withheld per KB-P12. Ticket T-6009 escalated. Employee is in chat now, reporting phone email failing and account locked.

args.note: Account E2901 locked after 11 failed sign-ins today from Bucharest, RO (no prior sign-ins from RO). New MFA device registered today 08:02 via self-service. Per KB-P12 no unlock, reset or MFA change performed. Escalated to Security on-call.

events.text:
Hi Brenda, I can't unlock your account right now. Here's why.

Your account was locked after a series of failed sign-in attempts this morning. Between about 7:00 and 9:40 AM today there were 11 failed attempts from Bucharest, Romania. You usually sign in from Portland, so this looks like a possible compromise. Also, a new authenticator device was added to your account at 8:02 AM today.

Under our security policy, I can't unlock the account, reset the password, or change MFA devices while a possible compromise is open. I've escalated this to the Security on-call team (reference SEC-500) and set your ticket T-6009 to escalated. Security will contact you, usually within an hour.

Until then:
- Please don't keep trying to sign in on your phone or other devices, since that adds more failed attempts.
- If you didn't add the "Android device" authenticator to your account this morning, tell Security when they contact you.
- If you're travelling or did try to sign in from Romania, let them know that too.

Oh no, okay. I'm not in Romania, I've been in Portland all week. I haven't added any new phone or device either, I only use my Pixel 8 for the authenticator. Nobody's asked me to set anything up.

I did get a couple of odd sign-in prompts on my phone this morning, I think they were around 8 or so? I tapped deny on both because I didn't recognise them. Is that related?

Also, how long will Security take? I really need my email on my phone for a meeting this afternoon.

args.note: Employee reports she is in Portland all week, has not added any device, and only uses her Pixel 8 authenticator. Nobody asked her to set anything up. She received two unexpected MFA sign-in prompts around 8 AM today and tapped deny on both. Her phone email is failing. She has a work meeting this afternoon. Security (SEC-500) to follow up.

events.text:
Yes, those prompts are very likely related. Someone who has your password is trying to sign in, and each prompt needs your approval on your phone. Tapping deny was the right move. Don't approve any prompts you didn't start, and don't share any codes.

Your account now has a second authenticator device that you didn't add, which is a strong sign that someone got into it. Only Security can safely clear that, so I can't unlock the account or change your MFA or password before they've checked it.

I've added your statement to ticket T-6009: you've been in Portland all week, you didn't add any device, and you denied the two prompts. Security responds within about an hour, so you should hear from them soon. I can't promise they'll finish before your afternoon meeting, because they need to check the account first.

For the meeting, you can use Outlook on the web in your browser or the desktop app on your computer, since you said your computer still works. If you need help getting into either, tell me and I'll walk you through it.

Okay, thanks. I'll stop trying on my phone and keep my eyes open for any more prompts.

Is there a number I can ring if Security doesn't get back to me before the meeting? I'd rather not wait around and miss something.

I don't have a direct phone number for Security, and I don't want to give you one I can't confirm. Here's what you can do:

- **Keep this chat open.** Security's follow-up is tied to ticket T-6009 (SEC-500), and I can add anything new you want them to know.
- **Check the internal directory or intranet** for the Security on-call contact if you need to call.
- **Ask me to escalate to a desk lead** if you haven't heard from Security well before your meeting. I can do that now if you'd like.

Until then, don't approve any prompts on your phone, and keep your laptop or the browser ready for your meeting.

Okay, thanks. I'll check the intranet for a Security number just in case, and keep this chat open. If I don't hear anything before my meeting, I'll ask for the escalation. I'll use Outlook on my laptop for now.

That sounds like a good plan. Security should be in touch soon, and I've logged everything you told me on ticket T-6009. If you don't hear back before your meeting, just message me here and I'll escalate it to a desk lead straight away. Good luck with the meeting, Brenda.
